summary: Tested the new Zyntha caption endpoint (POST /api/marketing/caption) end-to-end. Backend: 7/11 new caption tests PASS (validation 422 + 401 auth + ai_logs persistence + x platform happy path). 4/11 FAIL — instagram/facebook/linkedin/youtube happy-path tests return the RAW (unparsed/truncated) JSON string as the `caption` field, e.g. caption == '{"caption": "Big news! …'. Root cause: Gemini occasionally returns truncated JSON for longer outputs and `_coerce_caption_json` falls back to first-paragraph, which IS the truncated JSON fragment itself. Frontend wiring works correctly when Gemini returns valid JSON (verified with 'New vegan bakery opening in Amsterdam this Friday' — caption was cleanly extracted, 7 hashtag chips rendered, Copy button visible, empty-idea toast shown). Full regression: 51 passed, 4 failed (all the new bug), 1 skipped — pre-existing 44+1 baseline preserved.

critical.issue: When Gemini's response is truncated mid-JSON (reproducible with idea 'Just launched our new sustainable coffee blend' on instagram/facebook/linkedin/youtube), `_coerce_caption_json` fails json.loads and the except-branch returns the raw truncated JSON fragment as the caption (e.g. caption == '{"caption": "Big news! ✨ Our new sustainable coffee blend just dropped. \n\nCraf'). The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with caption that begins with '{"caption":' — exactly the failure mode the user wanted us to detect. Also returns hashtags=[] in that case.

integration_issues.issue: Works correctly when Gemini returns valid JSON. But because the backend bug above can return raw '{"caption":...' as the caption text, the user will sometimes see literal JSON inside the textarea after clicking Generate (no client-side guard). Add a backend fix; optionally a frontend guard that rejects/retries when caption starts with '{"caption"'.

action_items: Fix `_coerce_caption_json` in /app/backend/ai_assistants.py so a truncated Gemini reply never returns raw '{"caption":' as the caption. Recommended fixes (combine 2 of these): (a) Raise the Gemini max_tokens for caption from 600 → 1200 — current 600 is consistently being clipped for instagram/linkedin/youtube outputs. (b) When json.loads fails, try a regex extraction of the caption value: re.search(r'"caption"\s*:\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)', s) and unescape, then drop the unfinished tail and return that as the caption (with hashtags=[] is fine). (c) Pass a JSON response_format / response_mime_type='application/json' hint to Gemini via LlmChat.with_params so the model knows to emit a single JSON object.
Optionally add a guard in the endpoint: if result['caption'].lstrip().startswith('{"caption"') → retry once with a higher max_tokens, then 502 on second failure rather than returning broken text.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_assistants.py:469-473 — max_tokens=600 for caption generation is too tight. Gemini's JSON-mode replies for LinkedIn / YouTube routinely exceed this and get truncated mid-string, which is the direct trigger of the bug above.

ai_assistants.py:441-445 — the except-branch of _coerce_caption_json silently returns the raw truncated JSON as 'caption'. It should at minimum strip a leading '{"caption":' marker so the user never sees raw JSON.

server.py:700-723 — `marketing_caption` correctly avoids any plan gating (Starter can use it), uses Pydantic Literal for platform (422 on snapchat verified), and validates idea min_length=3 (422 on 'hi' verified). Good.
server.py:120-123 — CaptionIn correctly uses EmailStr-free Literal for platform; values match the 6 in the spec exactly.

MarketingContent.jsx — data-testid coverage is complete (mc-compose-textarea, mc-platform-select, mc-generate-caption, mc-hashtags, mc-copy-all). Empty-idea toast 'Type a few words about your post first.' triggers correctly and does NOT call the backend (verified).

rca of the issue:
Reproduction: POST /api/marketing/caption with body {idea:'Just launched our new sustainable coffee blend', platform:'instagram'} (or facebook/linkedin/youtube). Expected: caption is a clean human-readable string. Actual: caption is the literal string '{"caption": "Big news! ✨ Our new sustainable coffee blend just dropped. 

Craf' — i.e. raw JSON with no closing quote/brace. Mechanism: Gemini's reply exceeds max_tokens=600 and is truncated mid-string → json.loads throws → _coerce_caption_json's fallback emits cleaned.split('

')[0] which IS the truncated JSON because the unfinished string contains escape literals (`

`) not real newlines. Mitigation: bump max_tokens to ≥1200 and/or regex-extract the value of the 'caption' key even from a partial JSON string.
